brief.text:
The Engineering Leadership Journal is the private working record of the company's founder/CTO and engineering leader at a fintech. The company runs ACH money movement through sponsor bank Pillar, a round-up savings sweep, an investing product built on DriveWealth fractional shares, and planned card issuing. The notes cover mid-to-late 2026. They combine weekly 1on1 notes, skip-level notes, people profiles, daily logs, and personal reflections written during the Series B close. The central technical thread is the ACH pipeline rebuild and cut-over off legacy Rails/Sidekiq. The Sep 26 SEV1 sits inside that thread. It was an ACH double-debit caused by a missing idempotency key on the round-up sweep after a Sidekiq retry change. Devon Park's reconciliation job caught the double-debits within 47 minutes. The postmortem produced action items, and the card issuing soft launch slipped to Q1 2027. Investing GA received a no-go on 9/29 and still has open blockers, including DriveWealth position reconciliation following the Sep 15 position drift. The open risks are tracked by severity. They include round-up sweep on Sidekiq without idempotency keys through Q3 (severity 29), a late Q3 access review that could become a SOC 2 Type II exception (severity 29, owner Sam Whitfield, with an open todo for Sam to complete it), two GA blockers still open (severity 19), and a tight senior iOS offer on comp (severity 27, owner Nadia).

The people coverage is detailed. On the Payments team, Marcus Bell is the lead and Sarah Kim, Devon Park, and Sam are on the team. Marcus has been a single point of failure on the Pillar relationship. Sarah flagged this structurally, and the author had previously read it as a compliment. Marcus later handed the Pillar weekly sync to Sarah, and the author noted he seemed not fine. Devon is a senior backend engineer reporting to Marcus. He owns the ACH outbox worker, DriveWealth position reconciliation and alerting, and the deletion of the old Sidekiq ACH code. He built the shadow-mode diff harness for ADR-024, caught the April 6 anomaly, and wants to lead the ADR-032 build. The direct reports are Lin, Kavi, Nadia Okafor, and Renee. Lin is the sole designer. Her 1on1 settled on leading the investing tab with performance over portfolio value, cut auto-invest setup from 8 to 5 screens, and set up a quarterly design audit. Lin was told she is underpaid, with an adjustment coming after Series B. Kavi runs Growth and experimentation and is frustrated by the experiment freeze. The author reads this as frustration, not flight risk. Kavi owes pre-registration of the first three post-GA experiments. The manager owes Kavi an unfreeze date and a yes/no on copy-only tests. Nadia is the iOS/mobile lead and hiring manager. She is quietly checking senior iOS and EM market salaries, so her comp trajectory needs to be made explicit. Renee is driving the investing GA launch. Profiles also cover cofounder Aleks, partners, and two VP Engineering finalists.

The compensation and planning notes describe how the comp review will work. Bands get refreshed with post-close data from Jordan. The budget is set as a percent of eng payroll before Budget 2027 is finalized. Anyone past two years gets an equity refresh, and a named list is attached. There is also a flagged risk about how the incoming VP Eng affects this process. The founder reflections cover pressure from the Series B, the incident, and the board prep. They end with acceptance that this is the kind of hard year the author wants. Typical questions this region answers include what caused the Sep 26 double-debit, why Investing GA was no-go'd, what Devon owns, who runs the Pillar sync now, which team members are retention or comp risks, what commitments are owed from each 1on1, how the comp review will be structured, and which compliance and infrastructure risks remain open.
